title: <input type=url>: let authors declare the default scheme so users don't have to type https://
body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

In real-world forms (the "your website" field in profiles, registrations, contact forms), users type `ejemplo.com` and get a validation error, because `type=url` requires an absolute URL with a scheme. The usual outcome is frustration: the user doesn't understand why "their website" is invalid, or has to type an `https://` prefix they don't perceive as part of their site's name.

Browsers already solved this in the address bar with an implicit scheme plus visual confirmation. But form fields have no such mechanism, and the value is submitted as-is: a bare `ejemplo.com` simply fails there.

### What solutions exist today?

- `type=text` + `pattern`: loses all URL semantics (virtual keyboard, structural validation, autofill integration).
- JS normalization before submit: works, but every site reimplements it differently and inconsistently.
- The [prefixes and suffixes for textual inputs proposal (#10314)](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10314) covers the mechanics (a fixed `https://` prefix that is part of the value), but doesn't define its interaction with `type=url` validation.
- [#11083](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11083) shows that all three engines already validate `type=url` more leniently than the spec: the current definition is decoupled from real-world practice.

### How would you solve it?

Let the **author declare the expected scheme** per field, for example:

```html
<label>Your website
  <input type="url" name="web" scheme="https" required>
</label>
```

Proposed behavior:

1. The user types just `ejemplo.com`.
2. Before validation and submission, the browser completes the value: `https://ejemplo.com`.
3. Constraint validation operates on the **completed** value, which is an absolute URL conforming to the URL Standard — no change to the URL Standard itself.
4. `input.value` returns the completed URL.

**Why the declaration belongs to the author, not to a browser guess:** `type=url` legitimately accepts non-HTTP URLs (`ftp://intranet/file`, `mailto:contact@example.org`, internal hosts without a TLD). The browser cannot globally assume `https://` without breaking those cases or silently corrupting data — and omnibox heuristics are deliberately kept out of the standard for exactly that reason. The form author does know which scheme the field expects.

**Design points that would need defining:**

- Pasting a full URL (`https://ejemplo.com`) must not produce `https://https://ejemplo.com` — a normalization rule is needed.
- Undo, caret and selection behavior around the prefix.
- Communicating the full value to assistive technology.
- Interaction with autofill and `form.reset()`.

### Anything else?

Related: [#10314](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10314) (prefix mechanics), [#7794](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7794) (`input[mask]` — note: in the masking model the prefix is display-only and would not enter the value or validation; here the prefix must be part of the value), [#11083](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11083) (spec/implementation gap), [whatwg/url#531](https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/531) (context on scheme-less strings in the URL Standard).
